Master Services Agreement

between Quillon Freight Systems Ltd and Bexmoor Terminals plc
Dated 14 March 2026

Parties

(1) Quillon Freight Systems Ltd, a company incorporated in England and Wales under company number 09122447, whose registered office is at 14 Cranmoor Wharf, Bristol BS1 4QT (the "Supplier"); and

(2) Bexmoor Terminals plc, a company incorporated in England and Wales under company number 07741930, whose registered office is at Bexmoor Dock, Unit 3, Hull HU9 1PL (the "Customer").

Background

(A) The Customer operates bulk terminal facilities and requires inland haulage, container drayage and customs brokerage services.

(B) The Supplier has agreed to provide those services on the terms of this Agreement.

1. Definitions and Interpretation

In this Agreement the following expressions have the meanings set out below. "Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in England. "Charges" means the amounts payable under clause 6. "Services" means the services described in Schedule 1. Headings do not affect interpretation, and a reference to a clause is a reference to a clause of this Agreement.

2. Commencement and Term

This Agreement takes effect on 1 April 2026 and continues for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months, after which it renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives not less than ninety (90) days' written notice.

3. Supply of Services

The Supplier shall provide the Services with reasonable skill and care, in accordance with the service levels in Schedule 2, and shall allocate sufficient competent personnel and equipment to do so.

4. Customer Obligations

The Customer shall provide accurate consignment data not less than four (4) hours before each collection window, ensure safe site access, and hold all permits required for the goods presented.

5. Personnel and Subcontracting

The Supplier may subcontract any part of the Services to a subcontractor on its approved list, and remains liable for the acts and omissions of each subcontractor as if they were its own.

6. Charges and Payment

The Customer shall pay the Charges in Schedule 1 within thirty (30) days of the date of a valid invoice. Charges are exclusive of VAT. Rates are fixed for the first twelve (12) months and may then be adjusted once annually by no more than the change in the Consumer Prices Index.

7. Fuel and Surcharges

A fuel surcharge applies where the published weekly diesel index moves more than four per cent (4%) from the baseline of 148.20 pence per litre recorded on 1 March 2026. The surcharge is calculated monthly in arrears.

8. Late Payment

Interest accrues on overdue sums at four per cent (4%) above the Bank of England base rate, accruing daily from the due date until payment.

9. Service Levels and Service Credits

Where the Supplier fails to meet a service level in Schedule 2 in any measurement period, the Customer's sole financial remedy is the corresponding service credit, save in the case of persistent failure as defined in clause 10.

10. Persistent Failure

Three (3) or more service level failures of the same measure in any rolling six (6) month period constitute persistent failure, entitling the Customer to terminate the affected service line on thirty (30) days' notice.

11. Insurance

The Supplier shall maintain goods-in-transit insurance of not less than £2,000,000 per consignment and public liability insurance of not less than £10,000,000 in the aggregate, and shall produce certificates on request.

12. Liability

Neither party excludes liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence or for fraud. Subject to that, the Supplier's total aggregate liability in any contract year is limited to one hundred and twenty-five per cent (125%) of the Charges paid in that year.

13. Indemnity

The Customer shall indemnify the Supplier against all claims arising from inaccurate consignment data, misdeclared goods, or the presentation of goods requiring a permit the Customer does not hold.

14. Confidentiality

Each party shall keep confidential all Confidential Information of the other, use it only for the purposes of this Agreement, and return or destroy it on termination. This obligation survives for five (5) years.

15. Data Protection

Each party shall comply with applicable data protection law. The parties acknowledge that the Supplier acts as processor in respect of driver and consignee contact data, and Schedule 3 sets out the processing particulars.

16. Intellectual Property

All intellectual property rights in the Supplier's routing and telematics systems remain the Supplier's property. The Customer is granted a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence to use the tracking portal during the term.

17. Audit

The Customer may, on not less than fifteen (15) Business Days' notice and no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, audit the Supplier's records relating to the Charges.

18. Force Majeure

Neither party is liable for a failure to perform caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, provided it notifies the other promptly and uses reasonable endeavours to mitigate. Industrial action confined to the affected party's own workforce is excluded.

19. Suspension

The Supplier may suspend the Services where an invoice remains unpaid for more than forty-five (45) days, having given fourteen (14) days' written warning.

20. Termination

Either party may terminate immediately on written notice if the other commits a material breach that is not remedied within thirty (30) days of notice, or becomes subject to an insolvency event.

21. Consequences of Termination

On termination the Supplier shall complete consignments already in transit, return Customer property within ten (10) Business Days, and invoice for Services performed up to the termination date.

22. Assignment

Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, save to a member of its own group.

23. Notices

Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand or by recorded post to the registered office of the recipient, or by email to the address notified for that purpose. Email notice is not valid for termination.

24. Anti-Bribery and Modern Slavery

Each party shall comply with the Bribery Act 2010 and the Modern Slavery Act 2015, maintain appropriate policies, and notify the other of any breach affecting this Agreement.

25. Dispute Resolution

The parties shall first refer any dispute to their respective operations directors, and if unresolved after twenty (20) Business Days, to mediation under the CEDR Model Mediation Procedure before commencing proceedings.

26. Variation

No variation of this Agreement is effective unless in writing and signed by an authorised signatory of each party.

27. Waiver

A failure or delay in exercising a right under this Agreement does not operate as a waiver of that right.

28. Severance

If any provision is held invalid, it shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary, and the remainder of the Agreement continues in force.

29. Third Party Rights

A person who is not a party has no right under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999 to enforce any term of this Agreement.

30. Entire Agreement

This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior arrangements, save that nothing limits liability for fraudulent misrepresentation.

31. Counterparts

This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which is an original and which together constitute one instrument.

32. Governing Law and Jurisdiction

This Agreement and any dispute arising out of it are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales.
